_caveats: C1 is not a fair fight by design: G-dev sees k real labels and P sees none. It measures what the generic prior does with the labels each model already has for its dev gate, not which method is better in general.

TabPFN here is v2 (2025), on one CPU core with n_estimators = 2 and contexts of at most 1,024-2,560 rows. Current TabPFN (2.5 and later) and GPU-sized settings would likely do better. Read every G arm as a lower bound.

G-sim gives TabPFN 1,024 simulated rows. The released networks trained on the full banks of the same simulators: 12,473 to 28,744 rows in the pools drawn from here, and more for PlantDetective, whose 2,390-row pool holds only its full-year windows. C2 therefore compares learners on unequal amounts of the same data.
Each model is scored on its own exam with its own headline. The headlines are in different units and are never averaged across models; the cross-collection verdict is a count of per-model verdicts.

Only tabular models whose exam inputs, dev rows and simulated banks exist on this machine are in. Signal models (QuakeNet, ChirpNet, BeatNet's raw ECG) are out of scope, and so are tabular models whose data was not on this machine.

The exams were seen before: P's exam numbers are public. Nothing in this experiment was chosen from an exam label. Every setting came from dev or the frozen simulated set, and each model's pre-registration was hashed before its exam predictions.

Two contexts were capped for memory (Amendment A1). EnergyNet's G-dev holds 1,152 of its 1,496 dev trips, and its G-sim+dev holds 896 dev trips plus 256 simulated ones. So EnergyNet's C3 compares 896 dev labels plus simulation against 1,152 dev labels.

Expectations written before scoring (PREREG section 7) were half right. G-sim lost to P on most models, as guessed. But G-dev beat P on BDG2 with only 52 dev buildings, where we expected a loss. And simulated rows helped G-dev only on BasinDetective; they hurt on BDG2 and PlantDetective, where we expected them to help most.
gridpulse: Only 8 dev rows (4 events x 2 windows), so there is no learning curve. P reproduces the card (inertia MdAPE 14.5 % at N = 10 s, 16.4 % at N = 60 s). G-dev cannot learn inertia from 4 events, but it does well on MW lost at medium confidence. G-sim reads the same simulated events worse than the purpose-built network.
basindetective: Seven targets: the six out-of-period signature changes (Spearman rho) and regulated (AUC). P reproduces the card (rho 0.76 / 0.45 / 0.20 / 0.44 / 0.71 / 0.63). With 52 dev basins, TabPFN on dev alone loses clearly. Adding the 52 dev basins to 1,024 simulated basins recovers almost all of the gap, and it is the only model where the simulator rows help G-dev.
bldg_recs: 1,848 RECS dev homes is a large dev set for a 12-number input. P reproduces the card (floor area 33.6 %, heating group 87.3 %). Here the generic prior with dev labels wins clearly, and so does the card's own dev-fitted ridge/logistic baseline (C-dev). G-sim with 1,024 simulated homes slightly beats the released network.
bldg_bdg2: The BuildingDetective network reads use type badly on real buildings (14 %; card 14.4 %). With the 52 dev buildings, TabPFN doubles that (28.5 %) and cuts floor-area error from 49 % to 38 %. Mixing in simulated buildings hurts: the simulator's use-type mismatch is passed on to the in-context learner.
plantdetective: Read from a year of hourly output alone (the card's 'out' mode; the 'ctx' mode's EIA-860 table is not on this machine), on 2 year-windows per exam unit. With 60 dev windows from 40 units, TabPFN halves P's heat-rate error (9.8 % vs 21.3 %) and lifts technology accuracy from 69 % to 76 %. G-sim reads simulated plants into the real ones badly for technology (47 %). Adding the simulated rows to dev helps min load, ramp and starts, and hurts heat rate and technology.
energynet: VED exam trips, 8 per car (2,549 trips, 350 cars); P is scored on the same trips. P's ICE error here is 9.0 % (card, all 14,469 ICE trips: 8.6 %). With 1,152 dev trips from 16 cars, TabPFN ties P overall. It is better on hybrids (12.3 % vs 16.8 %), level on PHEVs and slightly worse on petrol cars. It takes the full dev context to draw level: at k = 320 it is still below P. Every learned arm beats the card's classical baselines, whose mean group MdAPE is 25.8 % (label economy) and 24.3 % (MOVES-like).
